prompt: Complete StudentSorter.sortByGradeThenName so it sorts a list of Student records in place by grade ascending, breaking ties alphabetically by name, using Comparator.comparing with thenComparing.
explanation: Comparator.comparingInt(Student::grade) builds a comparator from a key-extracting method reference, and thenComparing(Student::name) adds a tie-breaker that only applies when the first comparison says the grades are equal. Chaining factories like this replaces hand-written compare methods with a readable one-liner. list.sort(comparator) then sorts the list in place, so the method returns void.
hints: Start with java.util.Comparator.comparingInt(Student::grade) for the primary key.
Chain .thenComparing(Student::name) so equal grades fall back to name order.
Pass the finished comparator to list.sort(...); no return value is needed.
